capability: Scene list: a document as a row of independent patches, one active at a time
what_it_does: A show file is a row of self-contained patches called Scenes. Activating one starts all its actors and media; leaving it stops them. The row is the running order of the show.
max_check: Grepped obj-qlookup.json (core registry, 1,323 names) for 'scene' and 'cue': no names. Grepped the userguide for 'scene': only GL-scene and Live-API uses. Package library search 'scene' and 'cue': mo.cue (numbered cue trigger) and upshot_cues ('program cues'), neither a container of patches. Read refpages: pcontrol opens, closes and loads patcher windows; thispatcher setactivetab switches tabs; qlist stores timed messages. None starts and stops a whole patch with its media as a unit.
notes: The single largest gap. Everything a Max user builds by hand around poly~, pcontrol, mute and loadbang is the host's job here.

capability: Scene transitions with per-scene fade in, fade out and layering mode
what_it_does: Changing Scene crossfades the whole outgoing and incoming patch, video and sound together, over times stored on each Scene or given to the Jump actor. The new Scene can be added, drawn above or drawn below the old one.
max_check: Read refpages: jit.xfade crossfades two matrices; pattrstorage has 'fade' and 'recall' messages that interpolate stored parameter values. Neither fades two running patches against each other. No registry name contains 'fade' beyond these (jit.xfade found by grep 'xfade').
notes: Depends on the Scene model above; listed separately because the fade is the part operators use every cue.

capability: Secondary (background) Scenes with their own intensity
what_it_does: A patch can switch on other Scenes to run alongside the current one, each at its own brightness and volume, and they stay on across later Scene changes until switched off. Used for a continuous music bed, an always-on sensor or lighting patch, or parts of a heavy patch that run only when needed.
max_check: No registry or package hit for 'scene'. Max has no primary/secondary distinction because every loaded patcher runs; the closest practice is muting poly~ voices or subpatchers by hand. poly~ and mute behaviour taken from the repo's userguide notes (scans/userguide), not re-read this session.
notes: Max's everything-runs model covers the 'always on' case for free; what is missing is the managed on/off with a level.

capability: Cue numbering with point cues and renumbering
what_it_does: Each Scene carries a cue number separate from its position. Cues can be numbered by hand with decimals, or kept in order automatically with inserted cues getting point numbers such as 8.5. A patch or an operator button can go to a cue by number.
max_check: Registry grep 'cue': none. Package search 'cue': mo.cue ('set numbered cues and trigger events') and upshot_cues ('program cues'); only their library entries were read, not their patches. qlist refpage read: sequential message list, no numbering scheme.
notes: mo.cue may cover go-to-by-number; nothing found does insert-between numbering.

capability: Go Triggers: one document-wide GO / BACK binding for keyboard, MIDI and HID
what_it_does: One dialog binds next, previous, go-forward and go-backward to a key, a MIDI message or a learned HID button for the whole show. Go-forward and go-backward fire matching actors inside the active Scene, so the same button also steps through events within a cue.
max_check: Read the userguide topic mapping.json: Max 9 binds MIDI input or key presses to parameter-enabled objects, with learn. That covers binding a control to a button; it has no notion of next/previous cue. Registry has key, hid, gamepad.

capability: Cue Sheet: operator prompts that fire keys
what_it_does: Each Scene holds a list of cues with a line of text telling the operator what to wait for. Taking a cue shows the next prompt and sends that cue's key to the patch as if typed.
max_check: Registry and package grep for 'cue' as above; nothing presents a prompt list to an operator. Would be built from coll or qlist plus a display.
notes: Small feature; listed because it is a ready-made operator surface.

capability: Blind Mode: edit one Scene while another runs the show
what_it_does: Borrowed from lighting consoles. The operator opens and edits a different Scene while the active Scene keeps playing and keeps answering Go Triggers. The Scene being edited stays paused.
max_check: No registry or userguide hit for 'blind'. In Max any patcher can be edited while others run, so the live half exists; there is no way to edit a patch that is guaranteed not to execute, which is what blind means.

capability: Scene snapshots of every input, with per-actor opt-out
what_it_does: One click stores every input value of every actor in the Scene, with no set-up. Snapshots are recalled by click or by actor, and chosen actors can be told to ignore recalls.
max_check: Read refpages: preset stores and recalls user-interface objects' values; pattrstorage stores and recalls pattr presets and interpolates between them. Read userguide snapshots.json and presets_and_interpolation.json headings. Max is the stronger system (interpolation, files, priorities) but needs objects bound or named; Isadora captures every input automatically.
notes: Arguably Max is ahead here. Kept because zero-setup capture of all inputs is the difference.

capability: Automatic range scaling on every link
what_it_does: Each output has a range and each input has a range, and a value is mapped from one to the other as it crosses the link, with inversion by swapping the input's limits. Most connections need no scaling actor.
max_check: Max has the scale object (registry). Scaling is an object on the cord, not a property of the connection. zmap and parameter ranges not re-read this session.
notes: A design difference, not a missing function. Better in Isadora for beginners; hides the mapping from view, which Max's patch-is-the-documentation rule would dislike.

capability: Control Panels scoped to groups of Scenes, linked by Control ID
what_it_does: The operator interface is a separate panel whose controls reach actor inputs and outputs by ID number, not by cords. A panel belongs to a run of Scenes, so the interface on screen changes as the show moves on. Ready-made controls include a Scene list, GO and BACK buttons, a Stage thumbnail and a timecode display.
max_check: Max's presentation view is one per patcher; thispatcher setactivetab (refpage read) switches tabs. Nothing ties an interface page to a position in a show. Scene Select, Next Cue, Prev Cue have no counterpart because there are no Scenes.

capability: Bin Picker: clickable thumbnail grid of a media bin
what_it_does: A control that shows the files in a media bin as a grid of names or thumbnails; clicking one sends its number to any player. Media is addressed by index everywhere, so any number can pick a clip.
max_check: Read refpages: jit.playlist organizes video clips with a visual strip per clip; chooser is a scrolling list of selectable items. Neither is a thumbnail grid that feeds an arbitrary player. Only the first 650 characters of the Bin Picker entry were read.

capability: Run-only, password-locked show files with graded permissions
what_it_does: A document can be locked with a password so recipients can run it but not edit the patch. The author decides whether they may still edit the control panels, import media, or save.
max_check: Read userguide standalones_and_collectives.json headings: Max builds standalone applications and collectives. A standalone hides the patch but is a build, not a lock on an editable file with selectable permissions.

capability: Stages: numbered outputs decoupled from physical displays, saved per document
what_it_does: Patches render to a Stage number. A set-up window, saved with the document, says which displays make up each Stage, at what resolution, flipped or not. If a display is missing the Stage opens as a preview window, so the same file runs on a laptop and in the theatre. Virtual Stages are off-screen canvases at any size.
max_check: Read refpages: jit.world wraps a window, renderer and corner pin; its attribute list has fullscreen, rect, size, windowposition, enable_cornerpin, output_texture and no display-assignment table. jit.gl.node captures a sub-scene to a texture, the nearest thing to a Virtual Stage. Display assignment in Max is a window rectangle set per patch.

capability: Automatic edge blending from overlapping displays, with a wizard
what_it_does: Drag two displays of one Stage so they overlap and the overlap becomes a soft blend. Curve, gamma and knee are adjusted per edge. A wizard builds grids from 1x1 to 8x1 projectors from a resolution and an overlap. Mask actors do the same from inside a patch.
max_check: Grepped all refpages and bundled package docs for 'edgeblend' and 'keystone': no files. Userguide grep 'edge blend': none. Package library search 'blend' and 'edge': audio and geometry hits only. jit.gl.meshwarp (refpage read) has apply_mask and mask_mode attributes but no blend-between-projectors function.
notes: A shader in jit.gl.slab could do it; nothing shipped or installed does.

capability: IzzyMap: slice mapping inside every output, with every point drivable live
what_it_does: Each output actor contains a mapping editor. Regions of the source are cut out as triangles, quads, curved grids or compound masks built by adding and subtracting shapes, and placed on the surface. Slice position, opacity and individual point coordinates can be published as inputs and moved by sensors while the show runs.
max_check: Read refpages: jit.gl.meshwarp ('Video mapping tool', Jitter Tools package) deforms a texture on a 2D mesh with a mask and has meshdim, curvature, nurbs_order, mask_mode, save, read; jit.gl.cornerpin maps a texture by its four corners. Package search 'projection mapping': vs_output only. So one warped surface per object exists; a multi-slice editor with input and output views and compound masks does not.
notes: The composite-mapping KB article was fetched and not read.

capability: Dome and mirror warping from externally calibrated mesh files
what_it_does: Renders video through a warp mesh made by Paul Bourke's meshmapper, giving a correct image on a dome, cylinder or fisheye-mirror rig.
max_check: jit.gl.meshwarp refpage read: accepts a mesh_matrix and can read and save its own files. Whether it can load a Bourke-format mesh was not checked. Only the opening description of the Isadora actor was read.

capability: Media preloading handled by the host at every Scene change
what_it_does: Before a jump, Isadora reads which clips the next Scene will play, from where and at what speed, loads them in the background while the current Scene keeps running, and jumps only when they are ready. An actor can run the same preload early so a later cut is instant.
max_check: Refpage grep 'preload' found jit.polymovie, sfplay~, sflist~. Read jit.polymovie refpage: manages multiple jit.movie instances and preloads files for fast switching (Jitter Tools package). jit.movie has an asyncread message. Preloading exists per object; deciding what to preload from the next cue's contents does not.

capability: Record a Stage or camera and get the file back as playable media at once
what_it_does: An actor records a Stage or a live input to disk and, when stopped, places the new file in a chosen media slot, so the next actor can play back what was just recorded. Meant for live sampling of performers.
max_check: Read refpages: jit.record writes matrices to a movie; jit.vcr adds MSP audio; jit.gl.asyncread reads back the GL context. Recording exists. The record-then-appear-in-the-bin step is patched by hand (write, then read into jit.movie). The KB article was fetched and not read; its URL is from the enumerated index.

capability: Offline rendering by slowing the whole clock
what_it_does: A recording setting slows Isadora's internal clock to a percentage, so media and all time-based actors run slower and a heavy Scene records at full frame rate without dropped frames.
max_check: Read userguide non_realtime.json headings: it has sections for non-real-time audio and video. jit.record refpage: a realtime attribute, default off; when on, frames are written on a clock at the set frame rate rather than as each matrix arrives, which implies that with it off every arriving matrix becomes one frame. jit.world has a fixed_delta attribute (seen in its attribute list; description not read). So Max can render offline; the one-setting, whole-patch slowdown is the difference.

capability: One-checkbox Syphon, Spout, NDI and Blackmagic output per Stage
what_it_does: Each Stage or display can also be published to other applications or to capture-card outputs by ticking a box in Stage Setup, or by an actor that turns it on for one Scene.
max_check: Package library: Syphon package has jit.gl.syphonserver and jit.gl.syphonclient; Spout appears only through Vsynth modules that need a separate Spout package. Registry and package search for 'ndi', 'blackmagic', 'decklink': nothing installed. NDI output is claimed on the Site page; the manual documents only NDI input.
notes: Third-party NDI and Blackmagic externals for Max may exist but are not installed here, so not verified.

capability: Timecode as a data type, with MTC chase for movies
what_it_does: Timecode is a value type that converts itself to seconds, frames or text depending on what it is linked to, and compares correctly across frame rates. Actors read incoming MIDI Timecode, fire at a given time, and lock a movie to it by trimming speed and jumping when drift is too large.
max_check: Registry grep 'timecode', 'mtc', 'smpte', 'ltc': no names. Refpage grep 'time code' / 'MTC': only adstatus. Package library search 'timecode', 'mtc', 'ltc': nothing relevant. rtin refpage read: MIDI real-time messages (clock, start, stop), not quarter-frame timecode. transport and timepoint work in Max's own musical time.
notes: MTC quarter-frame messages could be decoded from midiin by hand. Only MTC input is documented for Isadora; no LTC.

capability: MIDI Show Control send and receive by named fields
what_it_does: Builds and decodes MIDI Show Control messages from named fields: device ID, command format, command, cue number, cue list, cue path, and timecode for timed commands. The sender's inputs change to match the command chosen.
max_check: Registry grep 'msc', 'showcontrol': none. Package search 'show control': none. sxformat refpage read: formats system exclusive bytes from arguments. MSC is sysex, so it can be assembled by hand; no object knows the protocol.

capability: PJLink projector control
what_it_does: Sends PJLink commands to a networked projector, with optional password, and outputs the projector's reply. Used to close the shutter between cues instead of projecting black.
max_check: Registry and package search 'pjlink': none. PJLink is a text protocol over TCP port 4352 (per the manual). Max's core registry has no TCP client: grep 'tcp' matched nothing, and 'net.' matched only jit.net.send and jit.net.recv, which carry matrices. sadam.tcpClient is installed (library entry read: 'Bidirectional TCP client'). max-mxj ships net.tcp.send and net.tcp.recv help files (seen by name, not read).
notes: Category is the nearest fit: projector hardware control.

capability: VISCA-over-IP camera control
what_it_does: Controls pan, tilt, zoom and focus of PTZ cameras that speak VISCA over IP or Datavideo DVIP, with range presets per camera model. Public beta, tested by the vendor on two models.
max_check: Registry and package search 'visca', 'ptz': none. Would be raw bytes over UDP or TCP. Only the first 2,300 of 21,700 characters of the actor entry were read.

capability: Art-Net DMX send and receive
what_it_does: Sends a DMX frame to an Art-Net node or broadcasts it, at a limited rate, and receives DMX so a lighting desk can drive the patch. Nodes on the network are listed in a menu.
max_check: Registry grep 'dmx', 'artnet', 'sacn': none. Refpage grep 'dmx': only a mention in serial. Package library: fxwdmxusbpro only (library entry read: sends DMX to an Enttec DMX USB Pro over serial). No Art-Net or sACN object is installed. udpsend refpage read: it has a rawbytes message, so Art-Net packets could be built by hand.
notes: Well-known third-party Art-Net externals exist for Max but none is installed, so none was verified.

capability: Lighting-style soft patch that crossfades with the Scenes
what_it_does: Cues send levels to logical channels. One receiver maps each logical channel to any set of output channels through an editable table, applies a grand master, and blends levels from two Scenes according to their fade progress, so a Scene crossfade is also a lighting crossfade. Output is formatted text for Art-Net, serial DMX or MIDI.
max_check: Registry has router and matrixctrl (names seen; refpages not read this session). pattrstorage refpage read: interpolates between stored presets, which is the nearest thing to a level crossfade. No object combines a patch table, a master and cue-driven mixing.
notes: Matrix Value Receive was read in full. Matrix Color Send, which samples pixel rows or columns of a video into the same channels for LED strips, was read in part; that sampling step alone is not a gap, since jit.spill ('Unroll a matrix into a list') and jit.iter exist in the registry. The soft patch with cue-driven mixing is the idea worth porting.

capability: BlackTrax (RTTrP) tracking input
what_it_does: Receives RTTrP packets from a BlackTrax performer-tracking system, by unicast or multicast, and outputs position, rotation, velocity and acceleration for a named trackable.
max_check: Registry and package search 'blacktrax', 'mocap': none. Would need a binary packet parser.
notes: Niche; relevant to large venues.

capability: Depth-camera skeleton tracking and a shared skeleton data type
what_it_does: One actor reads Kinect, Orbbec and RealSense depth cameras and outputs depth, colour, body masks and skeletons, and can record and replay depth streams. Skeletons travel as one value type that a decoder splits into named joints, a visualizer draws, a motion-capture suit also produces, and a JSON converter can feed from any other source.
max_check: Registry and package search 'kinect', 'openni', 'skeleton', 'pose', 'mediapipe', 'leap': nothing installed. cv.jit is installed and covers 2D image analysis, not depth skeletons. Only the opening of the OpenNI Tracker entry was read; the KB article URL is from the index and was not read.
notes: Third-party Kinect externals for Max exist but are not installed here. OpenNI Tracker is marked public beta with a long-run crash note.

capability: Leap Motion hand tracking
what_it_does: Reports the position and rotation of hands over a Leap Motion controller, and the angle and distance between two hands.
max_check: Registry and package search 'leap': none installed.
notes: Third-party externals may exist; not verified.

capability: Declarative parser for serial and TCP streams that creates named outputs
what_it_does: A watcher holds a pattern describing an incoming message: literal text, numbers of given width, hex, character sets, raw bytes, and bitfields with byte order. Each named element in the pattern becomes an output of the actor, typed as integer, float or text.
max_check: Read refpages: serial sends and receives bytes; regexp applies PCRE to symbols and lists. Parsing a device protocol in Max is a chain (serial, zl or match, itoa, regexp, unpack) or a script. Nothing turns one pattern string into typed, named outlets, and there is no bitfield extractor found.
notes: Read in full. Would port well as a v8 object.

capability: Raw TCP client in the core toolset
what_it_does: Opens a TCP connection to an address and port by stream number, sends formatted bytes, and parses replies, for talking to projectors, media servers and other show equipment.
max_check: Core registry grep 'tcp': no names. jit.net.send refpage read: sends matrices and messages to jit.net.recv over TCP, not arbitrary bytes to a third-party device. Installed Sadam Library provides sadam.tcpClient, sadam.tcpServer, sadam.tcpSender, sadam.tcpReceiver (library entries read). max-mxj has net.tcp.send / net.tcp.recv help files (seen by name).
notes: Available through a package, Java or Node; missing only from the core objects.

capability: Zero-configuration value sharing between machines on a LAN
what_it_does: Sends a number to other copies of the program on the local network by channel, addressed by a machine number set in preferences or to all machines, using multicast so no IP addresses are entered.
max_check: udpsend refpage read: needs a host and port. The bundled max-mxj package ships help files named net.maxhole, net.multi.send and net.multi.recv (found by listing the package's help folder; the help files were not opened, so what they do is taken from their names only). No core registry name suggests multicast.
notes: Probably covered by the mxj classes; the later pass should open net.maxhole.maxhelp to confirm.

capability: IzzyCast: internet video, audio and data sessions between patches
what_it_does: A host creates a session and others join by a session number. Each participant can send video, audio and control data to the others, and each incoming stream arrives as an ordinary video stream in the patch. Built on the Zoom Video SDK, so it needs no network set-up; paid by prepaid participant-minutes.
max_check: jit.net.send refpage read: matrices to a jit.net.recv at a known host and port, no relay or NAT traversal. Installed 'AOO for Max' package is audio over network (seen in the package list; its objects were not read). Nothing found carries video between remote patches through a hosted service.
notes: A paid hosted service, not a pure software feature. The IzzyCast feature pages were fetched and not read.

capability: RTMP streaming straight from a patch
what_it_does: Streams a video and audio feed to YouTube, Twitch, Facebook Live and similar services from an actor, given a stream URL and key.
max_check: Registry and package search 'rtmp', 'stream': no streaming objects. The usual Max route is Syphon or NDI into separate streaming software. KB article URL is from the index; fetched, not read.

capability: Text to speech as one object
what_it_does: Speaks a block of text with the operating system's voices, with voice, rate and volume inputs, an output device choice on macOS, and a trigger when finished.
max_check: Core registry grep 'speech', 'speak', 'tts': none. Package library: upshot_texttospeech ('text to speech engine'; library entry read, patch not opened).

capability: Speech to text as one object
what_it_does: Converts spoken audio into text inside the patch, for voice-controlled pieces. Added in an Isadora 4 point release.
max_check: Registry and package search 'speech to text', 'stt', 'whisper': none.
notes: Seen only as a heading and one sentence in the release notes; it is not in the v4.0 manual. How it works was not read.

capability: Subtitle playback from SRT files
what_it_does: Given a timecode position, normally a movie's, outputs the caption text from an SRT file for that moment, ready to draw over the video.
max_check: Registry and package search 'subtitle', 'srt': none. Would be a short script plus jit.gl.text.

capability: Embedded Python with virtual environments and pip packages
what_it_does: Runs Python scripts inside the patch in one long-lived interpreter, with inputs and outputs as script values, virtual environments, pip packages, and a per-show environment folder that travels with the file. Not sandboxed.
max_check: Registry grep 'python' and 'py': no Python object. Package library search 'python': none installed. Max's scripting hosts are JavaScript (v8, js), Node (node.script) and Java (mxj).
notes: Only the first tenth of the 38,000-character manual entry was read. Third-party Python externals for Max exist but are not installed here.

capability: Paste-in ShaderToy shaders with automatic inputs
what_it_does: A fragment shader is typed or pasted into the actor's editor and compiled on the spot. The compiler recognises ShaderToy code, so most shaders from that site run unchanged, and time and mouse inputs appear on the actor when the shader uses them.
max_check: Read refpages: jit.gl.slab processes textures with fragment shaders and exposes shader params (getparamlist, param); jit.gl.pass runs post-processing passes from a JXP file. Max shaders live in a .jxs XML wrapper that declares params and binds; grep of the Max install docs for 'shadertoy' found nothing. So the capability is there and deeper; the paste-and-run path is not.
notes: Only the first sixth of the KB tutorial was read. JitLygia is installed and may ease shader work; not checked.

capability: Triggers by wall-clock time and date
what_it_does: Fires at a given time every day, once at a given date and time, or periodically by the wall clock. For installations that open and close on a schedule.
max_check: date refpage read: reports current date and time when asked, so a schedule is a polling loop plus comparison. No registry name suggests a scheduler; timepoint works on transport time, not clock time.
notes: Small but common in installations.

capability: User Actors: embedded sub-patches that update every copy on request
what_it_does: A wrapped group of actors is stored inside the document yet keeps a shared identity. Closing its editor offers to rewrite every copy in every open document, keeping links and hand-set input values, or to split it off as a new variant. An on/off actor inside it stops its contents to save processing.
max_check: Max abstractions are files and update everywhere by nature; p subpatchers are embedded copies that never update each other. The embedded-but-synchronised middle case was not found. Based on the repo's userguide notes on abstractions and subpatchers, not re-read this session.

capability: Comparisons that report the moment they change, not only their state
what_it_does: Each comparison actor has three outputs: the 1 or 0 result, a trigger when the result turns true, and a trigger when it turns false. A 'notify' input chooses between sending the result on every input or only when it changes. Inside Range does the same for a low/high range, with 'enter' and 'exit' triggers.
max_check: Read refpages. `>` and `==` output 1 or 0 for every number received in the left inlet; neither has a change-only mode or an edge outlet. `change` passes a number only if it differs from the stored one. `togedge` bangs its left outlet on a 0-to-1 transition and its right outlet on 1-to-0. `split` sends in-range numbers left and the rest right, with no enter or exit event.
advice: In Max a comparison that drives an event needs two more boxes: put `togedge` (or `change` then `select 1 0`) straight under the `>`, or the event re-fires on every incoming number. For a range, feed `split`'s two outlets into `1` and `0` messages, then `togedge`.
notes: One Isadora actor does the work of three Max objects. The missing `change` is a common cause of events that fire continuously in Max.

capability: Threshold with a dead band built in
what_it_does: A threshold with separate low and high values. The output turns on above the high value and off below the low value, and nothing happens in between, so a noisy value sitting near one threshold does not chatter. It also sends a trigger for each crossing.
max_check: Searched obj-qlookup.json for 'hyst' and 'schmitt': no core object. Read `past`: one threshold, bangs when a number rises above it, and re-arms only after a lower number or a `clear`. `thresh~` is the signal-rate version (digest only read). The package library lists `dot.schmitt` (high and low thresholds, one trigger outlet), `mo.schmitt` and `dk.schmitt`.
advice: Never put a bare `>` or `past` on sensor data. Use `dot.schmitt` or `mo.schmitt` when the package is installed; otherwise write the two-threshold latch in a few lines of `v8`. A core-only abstraction for this is worth having.

capability: Named actors for 'nothing happened', 'too many at once' and 'all together'
what_it_does: Trigger Delay restarts its wait on every new trigger, so it fires only after triggers stop arriving. Multi Blocker passes the first value and drops any that follow within a set time. Simultaneity fires once when all of its trigger inputs have fired inside a time window.
max_check: Read refpages. `delay` holds a bang for a time and has `stop`; its refpage does not say what a second bang does while one is pending, and its help file has no comment on it either. `speedlim` passes a message only after a minimum time since the last one, with a `usurp` option to keep the newest. `buddy` waits until every inlet has received something, with no time limit. `thresh` and `quickthresh` collect numbers that arrive close together into one list.
advice: The nearest thing to Multi Blocker is `speedlim`; check in the patch whether a held message is dropped or sent late, since Multi Blocker drops. For 'all inputs within N ms' Max has no single object: `buddy` never times out, so add a `delay` that sends it `clear`, or do it in `v8`. For 'no input for N ms', test what `delay` does on a second bang in the patch itself before relying on it, since the refpage is silent.
notes: The `delay` re-trigger behaviour is the one thing here not confirmed from Max's own docs.

capability: Clock that pauses in place and deals its ticks round-robin
what_it_does: Pulse Generator fires at a frequency in Hz. Turning 'run/stop' off pauses it and turning it on continues from where it was in the cycle; 'reset' starts the cycle again. With several outputs it fires them in turn. Sequential Trigger and Trigger Divider do the round-robin and the divide-by-N on any trigger stream.
max_check: Read refpages. `metro` takes an interval in milliseconds or a note value, starts with a bang or non-zero number and stops with 0 or `stop`; there is an `active` attribute but no pause that keeps the position inside the interval. `cycle` sends each bang or number to the next outlet in turn, with `set` to choose the next outlet. `counter` counts bangs within a range.
advice: Round-robin triggers are `metro` into `cycle N`; a divider is `counter` into `select`. Note that Max thinks in milliseconds per tick and Isadora in ticks per second. If a pulse must resume mid-interval after a pause, Max needs a `v8` or signal-rate clock; `metro` always starts a fresh interval.

capability: Control-rate LFO as one object
what_it_does: Outputs a continuously changing number following a sine, square, triangle, sawtooth or stepped-random wave, at 0.0001 to 999 Hz. It has a phase offset, a reset trigger, and a 'once' mode that runs a single cycle per reset.
max_check: Searched obj-qlookup.json for 'lfo': no core object. The package library lists `mo.lfo~` (signal and data outlets), `vs_lfo` (texture and data, needs Vsynth's renderer) and `Abl.LFO~`. The core route is a signal oscillator sampled down to messages, which needs audio running; that part is from the repo's patching notes, not a refpage read this session.
advice: A message-rate LFO with shape, phase, reset and one-shot is worth building as a small `v8` object, so video and lighting patches do not need DSP switched on to animate a number.

capability: Multi-segment envelope that can advance one segment per trigger
what_it_does: A ramp of up to nine segments (99 in the ++ version), each with a time and a target value. A trigger mode chooses between running the whole envelope per trigger and running one segment per trigger, with an end trigger either per segment or at the end.
max_check: Read refpages. `line` takes a list of target-time pairs and has `pause`, `resume` and `stop`. `function` is a drawn breakpoint editor that outputs a list for `line`; breakpoints can be marked as sustain points, a bang plays up to the first sustain point and `next` continues from it. `bline` advances a ramp one step per bang.
advice: The Max match for 'one segment per trigger' is `function` with sustain points: bang to start, `next` on each later cue. The envelope is then drawn, not typed into eighteen inputs, which is the better editing surface. Use it for cue-stepped fades.

capability: Eased ramp with a speed limit, pause and a 'done' trigger
what_it_does: Ramps from a start to an end value over a duration along an s-curve whose steepness is one input. A 'max delta' input caps the rate of change, stretching the ramp when needed. It sends a trigger on completion; the 2D version ramps a point, with pause, resume and a 'moving' flag. Curvature bends any value along a two-control-point curve drawn on the actor.
max_check: Read `line` (linear ramps, pause and resume) and the installed ease package's `ease.maxref.xml`: `ease` applies a chosen easing function to an incoming float, with `input_range` and `output_range` attributes. It shapes a value; it does not generate the ramp. `function` has per-segment curve values (`setcurve`, `xyc`).
advice: Keep the two jobs apart in Max: `line` makes a linear 0-to-1 ramp, `ease` shapes it. That is more flexible than Isadora's single actor. What Max lacks is the rate cap: work out the time as distance divided by maximum speed before sending the pair to `line`.
notes: `ease` is a third-party package on this machine, not part of Max.

capability: Move toward a target at a fixed rate
what_it_does: The output moves continuously toward whatever target value it is given, at a set amount per second, and stops when it gets there. A new target simply changes where it is heading.
max_check: Searched obj-qlookup.json for 'slew': nothing at message rate. Read `slide`: it filters each incoming value by a formula applied per input, so it moves only when a value or a bang arrives and its speed depends on how often that happens. `line` reaches a target in a given time, not at a given rate.
advice: For constant-speed motion in Max, read the current value, compute time = distance / rate, and send target and time to `line`. Do not use `slide` for anything that must take a known time. A small 'seek' abstraction around `line` is worth keeping.

capability: Smoothing and decay that run on their own clock
what_it_does: Smoother filters a noisy number with one 0-to-1 smoothing amount and outputs at its own frequency, whether or not new input arrives. Decay Generator is a level that jumps up by a set amount on each trigger and falls at a set amount per second, giving a measure of how busy a trigger stream is.
max_check: Read `slide`: separate slide-up and slide-down values, and a bang 'performs the same function as float using the last input value'. It produces output only when it receives something. The package library lists `mo.smooth` (leaky integrator with up and down times in ms) and `dot.aggregate.leaky` (integrator with a leak).
advice: In Max, drive `slide` from a `metro` so it keeps settling after the sensor goes quiet; without the clock it freezes part-way. For an activity meter use `dot.aggregate.leaky`, or `accum` plus a clocked subtraction.

capability: Counter with a step size, limit-or-wrap, floats, and a settable current value
what_it_does: Adds or subtracts a set amount on its 'add' and 'sub' triggers, between a minimum and maximum. A mode chooses between stopping at the ends and wrapping. The current value is itself an input, so it can be preset or given a start value. Float Counter is the same with decimals.
max_check: Read refpages. `counter` counts whole numbers by one, up, down or up-and-down, between a minimum and maximum, with `set`, `jam`, `inc`, `dec` and carry outlets at the ends. `accum` stores a number and adds or multiplies into it, int or float, with no limits.
advice: Use `counter` for stepping through indexes; its up-and-down mode and carry outlets go beyond Isadora's. For a bounded float or a step other than one, use `accum` followed by `clip` or `%`, or `v8`. Do not force `counter` to do it.

capability: Toggle whose starting state is declared: on, off, or as last saved
what_it_does: A trigger-driven on/off switch with an 'init' input: 'on' or 'off' sends that state every time the Scene starts, and 'none' keeps whatever state was saved with the document.
max_check: Read refpages. `toggle` has no start-state attribute of its own; it has `parameter_enable` ('setting initial parameter values in Max'). `pattr` has `autorestore` (output the last-saved value at load) and `initial` (restore this value instead). `loadmess` sends a typed message at load.
advice: Decide for every stateful control in Max which of the three it is: always starts off (nothing needed), always starts at a value (`loadmess` through the control), or restores (`pattr` or parameter mode). Isadora makes the choice visible on the actor; in Max it is spread over three mechanisms, so say which one in a comment.

capability: Change filter with a minimum-change amount, that reports its value on start
what_it_does: Passes a value on only when it differs from the last output by at least a set amount, with a trigger alongside. When its Scene starts it sends the current input value once, so whatever follows begins in the right state.
max_check: Read `change`: passes a number only if different from the stored one; its modes report increase or decrease. There is no tolerance, so a float that jitters in its last digits passes every time. `round` rounds to a multiple of a given number.
advice: For noisy floats in Max, quantise before `change` (`round 0.01` then `change`), or write the dead band in `v8`. Also copy the second half: a filter that holds state should send it once at load, or the first real change is the first thing downstream ever sees.

capability: Running minimum and maximum, and self-calibrating ranges
what_it_does: Hold Range reports the lowest and highest value ever seen and the span between them. Calc Brightness has a measure trigger that watches a set number of frames and then rescales its output to the range it saw. Limit-Scale Value clips an input to one range and then maps it to another.
max_check: Read refpages. `peak` outputs a number when it exceeds the stored peak; `trough` does the opposite, and its stored value starts at 128. `scale` maps one range to another and its refpage says inputs 'are not clipped to this range'. `zmap` clips to its ranges but 'does not allow inverted scaling'.
advice: The Max calibration pattern is `peak` and `trough` feeding the input-range inlets of `scale`. Two traps: `trough` starts at 128, so send it a large value first, and `scale` overshoots outside its input range, so follow it with `clip` or use `zmap` when no inversion is needed.

capability: Selector that re-sends the chosen input's current value when the choice changes
what_it_does: Selector routes one of several inputs to one output. When the selection changes it immediately sends the current value of the newly chosen input, so the output is never stale. The inputs are typed by the first link made, and can carry video.
max_check: Read refpages. `switch`: a number in the left inlet 'specifies an open inlet for receiving subsequent messages'. It holds no values, so changing the selection outputs nothing until the newly opened inlet receives a message. `gate` is the same in the other direction.
advice: After changing a `switch` in Max, the output still shows the old source until the new one speaks. Where that matters, keep each source's latest value in an `int`, `float` or `pv` and bang the chosen one when the selection changes, or do the selection in `v8`.
notes: A frequent cause of 'the menu changed but nothing happened' in Max patches.

capability: Routing and bypass that stop the upstream work
what_it_does: Gate, Router and Selector have a hidden 'exec src' input. Set to 'gated', every actor upstream of a closed path stops executing, and the links turn red to show it. Separately, nearly every video effect has a 'bypass' input, Projector has 'active', and Movie Player has 'visible', which unloads the movie when off.
max_check: Read refpages. Max objects send messages onward when they receive them, so a closed `gate` below a chain does not stop the chain computing. `jit.gl.slab` has `bypass` ('the input is passed through to the output without processing'); `jit.gl.pix` lists `bypass` with no description. The GL group page gives every GL object `enable` ('drawing is enabled'). The matrix-operator group page lists no bypass attribute.
advice: In Max, close the path at the top: put the `gate` above the expensive chain, or stop the `metro` that drives it. A gate at the bottom saves nothing. Use `@bypass` on slabs and `@enable 0` on GL objects, and expose both where the operator can see them.

capability: Switching a whole sub-patch off from inside it
what_it_does: An actor placed inside a User Actor or Macro, with one 'enable' input. Off, every actor inside stops executing. Wired to a User Input, it gives the sub-patch an on/off input of its own.
max_check: Read refpages. `pcontrol`: 'the word enable followed by a 1 or a 0 will turn MIDI and Audio' on or off in connected subpatchers. `mute~` disables only the signal objects in a subpatcher. `poly~`'s `mute` turns off signal processing for one instance. None of them stops ordinary messages, timers or Jitter objects inside a `p` or abstraction.
advice: Give every heavy Max abstraction an enable inlet that gates its own clocks and inputs at the top, and sets `@enable` on its GL objects. For audio, load it in `poly~` and mute the instance. There is no one-box equivalent, so make it a convention.

capability: Sub-patch ports declared with a name, type, range and help text
what_it_does: Each port of a sub-patch is an actor whose dialog sets the port's name, data type (integer, float, trigger, on/off, video, a media file number and others), its minimum and maximum, and the help text shown on hover. Port order is set in a reorder dialog, not by where the actors sit. The sub-patch itself has its own help text.
max_check: Read `inlet`: its attributes are `comment` (the hover text, 'can only be set using the Comment setting in the inlet object's Inspector'), `cool` and a colour. No type or range. The userguide's subpatchers page says inlet order follows the position of the inlet objects, so moving one re-wires the parent.
advice: Max gives a port only a hover comment, so put the type and range in it ('float 0.-1.: mix') and clamp inside with `clip`. Keep inlets in a strict left-to-right row and never nudge one sideways past another. This is the repo's labelling rule; Isadora shows what it is standing in for.

capability: Wireless sends on numbered, typed channels that also carry video
what_it_does: Broadcaster sends any value, including a video stream, on a channel number. Every Listener on that number in any active Scene receives it. A Listener declares the type it outputs and converts to it, and has a trigger output beside its value. Their main documented use is passing values between Scenes that run at the same time.
max_check: Read `send` and `receive`: names, not numbers; any message; reaches every `receive` of the same name in every open patcher window. The repo's patching notes quote the refpage that the order two receivers fire in is not deterministic.
advice: Max's names are easier to read than channel numbers; keep them descriptive. The scoping differs: Isadora limits a broadcast to active Scenes, while Max's `s`/`r` reach every open patch, so anything loaded twice needs `#0` or `---` in the name.

capability: Named sets of global values that announce their own changes
what_it_does: A named collection of values that outlives Scene changes. Set writes the collection; any active Get with the same name outputs all the values whenever a Set is triggered, and also when its own Scene starts. Streams such as video are refused, and a trigger cannot be stored.
max_check: Read refpages. `value`: objects with the same name share one stored message, and 'you can get the contents out of a particular value object by sending it a bang', so readers are not told when it changes. `pv` is the same, limited to one patcher and its subpatchers. `dict` is a named store with keys.
advice: In Max a shared `value` is passive: pair it with an `s`/`r` of the same name when other parts of the patch must react to a change. For a named group of settings use one `dict`, not many `value` objects.

capability: A start value on any input, applied on activation and pushed through the patch
what_it_does: Any input can be given an 'Init' value that it takes each time its Scene starts. Since version 2 that value also makes the actor execute, so results travel downstream. Without Init, an input keeps the value it had when the Scene was left. Enter Scene Value and Enter Scene Trigger are the patched alternative.
source_urls: https://troikatronix.com/files/isadora-manual.pdf#page=483 (Actors Reference: Enter Scene Trigger / Enter Scene Value)
max_check: Read `loadmess` (sends its typed message at load, with a `defer` option), `loadbang`, and `pattr` (`autorestore`, `initial`). The userguide's patcher_lifecycle page says a patcher is initialised in phases, with objects created before any loadbang or loadmess fires, and subpatchers firing before their parents.
advice: A Max creation argument is Isadora's old behaviour: it sets the object silently and nothing downstream hears about it. When later objects or displays must start in agreement, send the value through the control with `loadmess`. When they need not, the argument alone is enough and an extra `loadmess` is clutter.
notes: The Isadora author's own account of why silent initial values caused trouble is in the KB article.

capability: Evaluation by pulling from the end of each chain, top-to-bottom for ties
what_it_does: Isadora works in cycles. Each cycle it starts from actors at the end of a chain and executes whatever is upstream of each input. When several links feed one input, the upstream actors run from top to bottom of the screen and the last one to produce a value wins. Every input holds its latest value, and a trigger input fires when any new value reaches it.
max_check: The repo's `patching/MAX_PATCHING.md` (promoted from Max's userguide) says Max walks the graph depth-first within one event and that `trigger` fires right to left; the repo's `CLAUDE.md` quotes `trigger`'s refpage for the same order. Neither page was re-opened this session. Max pushes each message as it happens; there is no per-cycle pass and no stored value on a cold inlet until something sets it.
advice: Do not carry Isadora habits into Max: position on screen is not a safe way to order things, several cords into one inlet arrive as separate events, and an inlet has no value until it receives one. Make order explicit with `trigger`, and convert values to bangs explicitly with `t b`.
notes: The KB article describes version 2; the v4 manual does not restate the algorithm.

capability: Table actor with read-on-start and write-on-exit file modes
what_it_does: A list of lines, each with a set number of numeric or text items, with one input and one output per item. Lines are added, inserted, replaced, deleted and recalled by number. A tab-separated text file can back it, with a mode that reads on activation, writes on deactivation, both or neither, and a switch for keeping a copy inside the document.
max_check: Read refpages. `coll`: when a patch with a named coll loads, Max looks for a file of that name and loads it; `embed` saves the data in the patcher; `write` and `writeagain` save on request. `dict` takes a file name as an argument to import on load and has `embed`. `closebang` sends a bang when its patcher window closes. Nothing writes back by itself.
advice: In Max say where the data lives: `@embed 1` for data that belongs to the patch, a named file for data that outlives it. For write-on-exit, wire `closebang` to `writeagain`. `coll` returns a whole line as a list, so follow it with `unjoin` to get Isadora's one-outlet-per-column.

capability: Text as its own value type, with small actors for cutting and joining
what_it_does: Text is a link type. Small actors take the first, last or middle characters or lines, append to a growing string, wrap at a line length, compare two strings with or without case, and build formatted text from up to nine parameters.
max_check: obj-qlookup.json lists about forty `string.*` objects in Max 9 (append, compare, contains, indexof, length, replace, slice, split, sprintf, substring, tolower, trim and others). `string`'s refpage calls a string 'a block of text in memory that is not stored in Max's symbol table', and the userguide's strings page says the purpose-built String objects are easier and more efficient for text work than symbols. Also read the digests of `string.sprintf`, `string.split` and `string.substring`.
advice: In Max 9, treat text that changes while the patch runs as a `string`, not a symbol, and reach for `string.*` before `sprintf` and `regexp` chains. Max is now at least level with Isadora here, but only if the new family is used.
notes: Only four of the string objects' pages were opened; the rest are known by registry name.

capability: Keyboard watcher with a key range, key names and press/release choice
what_it_does: Keyboard Watcher is set to a key or a range of keys, written in quotes, with names for special keys such as 'right-arrow', and to press, release or both. Key Table Watcher holds up to 32 keys and outputs the position of the one pressed, which turns a row of keys into a selector.
max_check: Read `key` and `keyup`: no inlets and no filter; four outlets give the ASCII code, a platform-specific key code, the modifier keys and a platform-independent key code. The userguide's mapping page describes Max 9 Mappings, which bind key presses or MIDI to parameter-enabled objects with no patching.
advice: In Max filter keys with `select` under `key`, and take the fourth outlet when the patch must behave the same on Mac and Windows. For operator shortcuts, prefer Max 9 Mappings: the binding is then visible and editable outside the patch, which is what Isadora's Go Triggers give.

capability: Mouse position as a percentage of a region, gated by modifier keys
what_it_does: Reports the mouse as 0 to 100 percent across a chosen part of the display, only while a chosen set of modifier keys is held, with a trigger on each move. The Stage version does the same inside one output window and adds click triggers, an inside/outside flag and scroll-wheel values.
max_check: Read refpages. `mousestate` reports position in pixels plus deltas, buttons and wheel, on a bang or after `poll`, with a `mode` message for the coordinate reference; its description limits it to when the cursor is in a Max patcher window. `modifiers` reports modifier keys on a bang or at a polling rate. `jit.window` and `jit.world` report mouse events on their window from the dump outlet; `jit.window` has `idlemouse` to include movement without a button.
advice: For interaction on the video output in Max, take the mouse messages from the `jit.world` dump outlet, not from `mousestate`, and divide by the window size so the patch survives a change of resolution. Gate with `modifiers` and a `gate`.

capability: MIDI input actors with a range filter on every field
what_it_does: Each MIDI watcher takes a single value or a range for port, channel, and the message's own fields (pitch and velocity, or controller and value). A message must fall inside all of them to be seen. The outputs give the matched values and a trigger.
max_check: Read `notein`: arguments choose a port or device and a channel; outlets are pitch, velocity and channel, with no range filter. `stripnote` passes only note-ons. `split` passes a number range. `midiselect` separates a raw MIDI stream by attribute.
advice: In Max the filter is patched after the input: `notein` to `stripnote` to `split`. That is one more box per condition, but each condition is visible on the patch, and a `kslider` or `live.dial` can sit in the path to show what arrived.

capability: Note sender that owns its note-offs
what_it_does: Send Note sends a note-on per trigger and, if a duration is set, the matching note-off later; a 'quiet' switch silences the previous note first. All Notes Off sends note-offs only for notes Isadora knows are sounding. Mini Sequencer plays one of a list of pitches per selection and silences the last one on leaving the Scene.
max_check: Read refpages. `makenote` pairs a pitch with a velocity and sends the note-off after a duration; `stop` sends note-offs for everything it holds, `clear` forgets them, and `repeatmode` sets what a repeated pitch does. `flush` and `midiflush` track note-ons passing through and send the missing note-offs on a bang.
advice: Same idea in both tools. In Max route every generated note through `makenote`, or put `flush` before `noteout`, and send `stop` or a bang whenever the transport or the section stops. Isadora does this on leaving a Scene; Max will leave notes hanging unless it is wired.

capability: OSC listener with wildcards, a backlog counter and a choice about dropping
what_it_does: OSC Address Listener matches an address pattern with * wildcards and outputs the values, the matched address and a JSON copy of the message. A 'one per cycle' switch chooses between always showing the newest message, dropping any that arrive faster than the patch runs, and queueing every message, with a 'pending msgs' output showing the backlog.
max_check: Read refpages. `udpreceive` has one data outlet, a `maxqueuesize` message, `defer` and `outputformat`. `osc.packet` stores an OSC packet and converts formats. `param.osc` maps OSC onto a patch's parameters. The package library lists `o.route` as the current address router and marks CNMAT's `osc-route` deprecated. `qlim` and `speedlim` limit message rate.
advice: Max makes no drop-or-queue decision visible. On any high-rate OSC stream, decide it yourself: `speedlim` or `qlim` after `udpreceive` for 'newest wins', and know that `maxqueuesize` exists. Use `o.route` for address patterns.
notes: What `udpreceive` does when its queue is full was not read.

capability: Movie play segment as start plus length, with position measured inside it
what_it_does: The part of a movie that plays is set by 'play start' and 'play length', both as a percentage of the file. The 'position' input jumps within that segment. Loop is off, on or palindrome. Outputs give a trigger per new frame, a trigger at each loop end and the position. Helper actors convert between seconds and percent for a given file.
max_check: Read refpages. `jit.movie`: `looppoints` in the movie's time units, plus `looppoints_ms` and `looppoints_secs`; `position` is normalised 0 to 1 over the whole movie; `loopreport` sends `loopnotify` at the loop point (both ends in palindrome); `unique` outputs only new frames; `rate` sets speed. `jit.playlist`: `selection <clip> <start> <end>` in a normalised range, `selectionms`, `loopreport`, `reportprogress`.
advice: In Max state loop points in seconds (`looppoints_secs`) or use `jit.playlist`'s `selection`, and turn on `@loopreport 1` and `@unique 1` to get Isadora's loop-end and new-frame triggers. Max's `position` covers the whole file, not the loop, so rescale it when scrubbing inside a loop.

capability: Codec advice tied to how the clip will be played
what_it_does: The documentation gives one rule: clips that are scrubbed, reversed, sped up or looped tightly should use a codec that stores every frame whole (HAP, ProRes, Photo JPEG), and H.264 is only for playing straight through at normal speed. It also asks for one codec, one resolution and one frame rate per project, with the target frame rate matched to the display's refresh rate.
max_check: Listed Max's bundled packages: `hap` and `VIDDLL` are among them. Read `jit.movie`: the `engine` attribute chooses the video backend (avf, qt or viddll) and can only be set in the box. Max's own codec guidance was not read this session.
advice: The rule is about codecs, not Isadora, so apply it in Max too: before debugging stutter in a `jit.movie` that scrubs or runs backwards, check the file's codec. Keep one codec and one frame rate per piece.

capability: A premultiplied-alpha flag that travels with the video stream
what_it_does: Every video stream with an alpha channel carries a flag saying whether its colour is already multiplied by its alpha. Movie Player sets it per movie, and Alpha Tool can flip the flag or actually convert the image. The manual's symptom to look for is a light or dark halo on soft edges.
max_check: Searched every Max refpage for 'premult': no hits. The GL group page documents `blend` as named modes over `blend_mode` source and destination factors, where `alphablend` is `6 7` (source alpha, one minus source alpha) and factor 1 is 'one'.
advice: Max leaves this to the patcher. Dark fringes on soft edges usually mean a premultiplied source drawn with `alphablend`; try `@blend_mode 1 7` on that layer. Note in a comment which kind each source is, because nothing in Max carries the information.
notes: The `1 7` setting is worked out from the factor table in the refpage; it was not tested in Max.

capability: Output layer with three blend choices and one 'intensity' input
what_it_does: Projector draws a stream on a Stage with a 'layer' number and a 'blend' of additive, transparent or opaque. One 'intensity' input means brightness under additive and opaque, and opacity under transparent, so a fade is always the same input. The manual warns that a transparent image must be on a higher layer than what it sits over.
max_check: Read the GL group refpage and Max's transform-defaults registry. `layer`: 'the layer number determines the rendering order (low to high). Objects in the same layer have no guarantee which will be rendered first.' `blend` has eight named modes (add, multiply, screen, exclusion, colorblend, alphablend, coloradd, alphaadd). `jit.gl.layer` loads with blending on and depth testing off; `jit.gl.videoplane` with blending off and depth on.
advice: Max offers more blend modes but no single fade input. Use `jit.gl.layer`, give every one an explicit `@layer`, since equal layers draw in no fixed order, and fade with the alpha of `color` under `alphablend` or by scaling `color`'s red, green and blue under `add`.

capability: Keyers and masks that can output transparency instead of a finished mix
what_it_does: The two keyers normally output foreground mixed over background. With their 'alpha' switch on they output the foreground with a transparent hole, for the Projector to composite over whatever is on lower layers. Add Alpha Channel attaches any stream as another stream's alpha. Alpha Mask mixes two streams by a third and has a 'strength' input for fading the mask in.
max_check: Read refpages. `jit.chromakey` and `jit.lumakey` take `tol` and `fade` and have a `mode`: 0 performs the key and outputs the mix, 1 outputs the key map 'for use elsewhere'. `jit.alphablend` crossfades two matrices by the alpha plane of the left one. These are CPU matrix objects.
advice: In Max, prefer keying to alpha and letting `jit.gl.layer` do the mix: take the key map (`@mode 1`), use it as the alpha of the foreground, and layer it. That keeps the background free to be anything on a lower layer, which is the design Isadora's 'alpha' switch points at.

capability: A stated rule for mixing streams of different sizes
what_it_does: When two streams of different resolution meet, one is scaled to match. A preference sets the default rule, and Video Mixer's 'frame scale' input can override it per actor: largest, smallest, or the minimum or maximum width or height. The manual tells users to keep every stream the same size because the scaling costs time.
max_check: Read refpages. `jit.gl.slab` and `jit.gl.pix`: `adapt` (default 1) makes the output size match the input; with it off, `dim` sets the size, and `dimscale` multiplies it. `jit.xfade`'s own page lists only the crossfade amount; the matrix-operator group page gives every such object `adapt`.
advice: In Max the output size of a two-input slab follows an input unless told otherwise. Where sources differ, set `@adapt 0 @dim <w> <h>` on the mixing object so the size is a decision written on the box, and keep every source at that size upstream.
notes: Which input `adapt` follows on a multi-input slab was not read.

capability: Frame bank and video delay as single actors
what_it_does: Buffer stores a set number of frames in turn and outputs whichever one its 'select' input names, with a mode that stops when full and a trigger when the last frame is stored. Video Delay is a chain of frames of a set length. Freeze holds a frame while a switch is on, or grabs one on a trigger.
max_check: Read `jit.matrixset`: a set of `matrixcount` matrices; `index` chooses which one an incoming matrix is written to; `thru` passes input on; it can import and export movies. A refpage exists for `jit.gl.textureset` ('mimics the functionality of jit.matrixset but outputs textures'), but that name is not in the core obj-qlookup.json, so whether it loads here was not confirmed.
advice: In Max the frame bank is `jit.matrixset` with a `counter` on `index`; the 'stop when full' and 'last frame' signals come from the counter's carry outlet. Check that `jit.gl.textureset` instantiates before planning a GPU version around it.
notes: How a stored matrix is read back out of `jit.matrixset` was not read; only the write side is described above.

capability: Sample player with numbered voices and routing written as text
what_it_does: Sound Player loads a file into memory and plays it on one of 16 'sampler channels'. A second sound on the same channel cuts the first off; different channels overlap; channel 0 picks a free one. Routing from file channels to device outputs is one text input such as 's1:d3, s2:d4@-3dB', so another actor can compute it. Loops have a crossfade length in samples.
max_check: Read refpages. `playlist~`: clips with a `selection`, `loop`, `speed`, `channelcount` and `loopreport`. `groove~`: loop points, and `loopinterp` for interpolation around them. `matrix~`: any inlet to any outlet with a gain, set by `connect` or list messages, a `ramp` time to avoid clicks, and a dictionary form of its whole state. `poly~` has voice allocation and a `steal` attribute.
advice: Max splits this into parts, and each part is stronger: `poly~` for voices and stealing, `matrix~` for routing. Keep all routing in one `matrix~` with `@ramp`, driven by messages, so a routing can be stored and recalled as data, which is what Isadora's routing string is for.

capability: Audio level watcher with a noise floor that rescales, and a trigger level
what_it_does: Reports the level of a live input as 0 to 100. A 'min level' input sets a floor: below it nothing is sent, and above it the output is rescaled so the floor reads 0. A 'trig level' input fires a trigger each time the level rises past it. The frequency versions do the same for one band or for a run of FFT bands.
max_check: Read refpages. `peakamp~` reports the peak amplitude since its last report, at an interval in ms. `zmap` maps and clips a range. `past` bangs when a number rises above a threshold. `thresh~` detects a signal above a set level (digest only).
advice: The Max chain is `peakamp~ 50` to `zmap <floor> 1. 0. 1.` to a threshold with a dead band. Copy the floor-and-rescale step: without it a quiet room never reads zero and every mapping after it is offset.

capability: Live inputs as shared numbered channels, configured in one window
what_it_does: Camera and audio devices are assigned to four capture channels in one settings window. A patch only names a channel number: Video In Watcher outputs its video, and Capture Control starts or stops it. Any number of watchers can read the same channel, and moving to another machine means re-assigning devices in one place.
max_check: Read `jit.grab`: each object opens a device itself (`open`, `close`), chosen with `vdevice`, `input` and `format`; `getvdevlist` reports the devices; `uniqueid` is 'the unique ID string for the currently selected video device' and 'remains consistent'; `output_texture` gives a texture; `unique` passes only new frames.
advice: In Max keep one `jit.grab` per camera, in one place in the patch, and share its output by name, so the device choice exists once. Fill a `umenu` from `getvdevlist`, and store `uniqueid`, not the list index, so the right camera is found after a re-plug.

capability: Text renderer that reports the size of what it drew
what_it_does: Text Draw renders text into a video stream inside a bounding rectangle with padding, alignment, line spacing, a scroll position and a background colour. A 'measure mode' turns on outputs giving the rendered text's position, width and height, in units chosen to match the Shapes actor, so a box can be drawn to fit the words.
max_check: Read `jit.gl.text`'s attribute list: `align`, `fontname`, `fontsize`, `leadscale`, `line_length` (wraps lines past this length), `tracking`, `screenmode`, `depth`. No attribute or message in the list reports the size of the rendered text.
advice: In Max, fix the box and make the text fit it: set `line_length` to wrap and size the backing shape from that, not from the text. If a caption box must hug its text, check `jit.mgraphics` or a `v8ui` script for text measuring first; neither was read here.
notes: Only the names in `jit.gl.text`'s refpage were checked; a measuring feature under another name would have been missed.

capability: Menus and lists that fill themselves from the options of what they control
what_it_does: A Popup Menu or List Selector control linked to an input that has a fixed set of options, such as a blend mode or a list of available NDI or Syphon sources, can fill its item list from that input. The list can also be sent to the control as text, one item per line, from any actor output.
max_check: Read refpages. `attrui` inspects the attributes of the object it is connected to: a menu chooses the attribute and the right half shows a control for its value. `umenu` items are typed in the Inspector, set by messages or a dictionary, or filled from a folder with `autopopulate` and `prefix`.
advice: Max already has this for real attributes: use `attrui`, which shows an attribute's own option list, in place of a hand-typed `umenu` that can drift from the object. For lists that only exist at run time (devices, files), have the source send its list and fill the `umenu` from it.

capability: Controls that follow the value they control
what_it_does: Every control has a 'Show Value of Linked Properties' option. With it on, when anything else changes the linked input, the control moves to match. A control linked to an output always shows that output. With several links the newest value wins.
max_check: Read refpages. `attrui` shows the current value of the attribute it controls. `toggle` (and other UI objects) list `param_connect`: 'a two-way connection between the object and a parameter of a compatible object ... such as gen~ or jit.gl.slab ... will update if the parameter value changes'. `pattr` can bind to a named object and share its value.
advice: In Max a control shows the truth only if it sits in the path of the value or is bound to it. Prefer `attrui` and `param_connect`; otherwise put the UI object in series so every source passes through it. A slider beside the data, fed nothing, shows only what the operator last did.

capability: Button control with its own on and off values, two modes and a display-only flag
what_it_does: A Button sends a chosen 'On Value' and 'Off Value', not just 1 and 0. It is momentary or toggling, can be told never to send the off value, can swap the two, and has separate text and colours per state. A 'Display-Only' option, also on Slider, makes it ignore clicks so it serves as an indicator.
max_check: Read refpages. `live.text`: `mode` 0 button or 1 toggle, `text` and `texton` labels, `active`. `textbutton`: the same two modes, plus `outputmode` for sending on mouse down or mouse up. `ignoreclick` is listed in the common box refpage (`jbox`). Neither button has settable output values.
advice: In Max use `live.text` and translate its 1 and 0 with a message box or `select 1 0` directly underneath. For indicators set `ignoreclick 1`, and describe the box as display-only in its label so nobody clicks it.

capability: Text entry control with a key filter, length limit, single-line and password options
what_it_does: The Edit Text control can be limited to integers, floats, hexadecimal or letters and digits, to a maximum number of characters and to one line. It can be read-only, can show bullets for passwords, and has start-up text. Set Control Focus moves typing to a named control, for forms with several fields.
max_check: Read `textedit`'s attributes: `outputmode` (message or single symbol), `keymode`, `lines`, `readonly`, `tabmode`, `separator`, `wordwrap`, `clickmode`, `autoscroll`, `nosymquotes`. A search of the same list for 'password', 'maxchar' and 'filter' found nothing. `dialog` opens a box that returns one symbol.
advice: Do not ask `textedit` to validate; it cannot. For a number use a number box, for a fixed set a `umenu`, for a one-off string a `dialog`, and check free text in `v8` before it is used. This is the repo's `textedit` rule seen from the other side.

capability: Showing and hiding groups of controls by a name pattern
what_it_does: Every control has a text 'Control Address'. Show-Hide Control shows or hides every control whose address matches a pattern with * and ? wildcards, on Scene entry or when its 'visible' input changes. Naming controls '/page1/...' turns one panel into several pages.
max_check: Read `thispatcher`: it evaluates patcher and scripting messages (the page points to a separate discussion of them, not read) and has `setactivetab`, which changes the active tab of a tabbed patcher by the name shown on the tab.
advice: For pages of controls in Max, use patcher tabs and `thispatcher setactivetab`, where each page is an ordinary subpatcher and nothing is hidden. Scripted show and hide needs names, a controller and state to keep in step, which is the cost Isadora's pattern-matching hides.

capability: Performance figures as values inside the patch and on the operator panel
what_it_does: Performance Monitor outputs the target frame rate, the actual frame rate, the patch cycles per second and the share of time spent on video. An FPS control puts the frame rate on the operator's panel. Monitor and Stage Preview show any stream or a whole output as a thumbnail with a frame-rate cap. Grapher plots values over time as a video stream.
max_check: Read refpages. `jit.fpsgui` displays fps, ms per frame, and a matrix's type, dimensions and plane count for whatever passes through it. `jit.world`: `getrunning_fps` 'will return the actual frames per second rendered by this context'. The userguide's debugging page describes event, signal and matrix probes on patch cords, enabled from the Debug menu.
advice: Put a `jit.fpsgui` in the presentation view of any show patch, and poll `getrunning_fps` to raise a visible warning when it falls below target. Max's probes cover Isadora's hover-over-a-link preview, but only while editing.

capability: Stopwatch with run, pause and reset
what_it_does: Outputs elapsed time continuously. Three triggers run it, pause it and reset it to zero; after a pause, run carries on from the paused time.
max_check: Read refpages. `timer` reports the time between a bang in its left inlet and a bang in its right. `clocker` reports elapsed time at an interval, with start, `stop` and `reset`; a bang while stopped starts the count and a bang while running resets it. Neither has a pause that keeps the elapsed time.
advice: A pausable show clock in Max needs an accumulator: add each `clocker` run to an `accum` when it stops, or keep the start time and the paused total in `v8`. Worth a small reusable object, since every show patch wants one.

capability: Tap tempo with averaging
what_it_does: Tap Tempo measures the rate of incoming triggers and outputs it in beats per minute and in Hz, averaged over a chosen number of taps. Loop Calculator turns tapped tempo into a loop length for a given movie or sound.
max_check: Searched obj-qlookup.json for 'tap': only delay-line taps. `tempo` generates a metronome from a BPM; it does not measure one (digest read). `timer` gives the time between two bangs. The package library lists `upshot_transport` with a tap-tempo inlet.
advice: In Max build it from `timer`: feed one bang to both inlets through `t b b`, average the last few intervals, and take 60000 divided by the mean. Worth keeping as an abstraction with the tap count as an argument.

capability: Media addressed by a number in a shared bin
what_it_does: Every player actor names its file by an index into the document's Media View. Three actors count the items in a bin, convert bin and item numbers to that index, and return the file name. The show moves to another machine by keeping media folders beside the document. Picture Player sends a frame only when the picture, visibility or Scene changes.
source_urls: https://troikatronix.com/files/isadora-manual.pdf#page=503 (Actors Reference: Get Media Count / Get Media File Name)
max_check: Read refpages. `folder` lists the files in a folder, 'especially useful for loading a umenu'. `umenu`: `autopopulate` with a folder path as `prefix` fills it at load, filtered by `types`. `jit.playlist`: a number plays the clip with that index, counting from 1; `playlist~` numbers its clips from 1 in its `selection` and `setclip` messages. `polybuffer~` names its buffers by index.
advice: Max has no media bin, so build the index once: a `umenu @autopopulate 1` on a media folder beside the patch, or one `jit.playlist`. Then address clips by number everywhere else. Keep the folder next to the patch so the piece moves as one directory.
